identity.note: Prefix namespace for this product's entity types (governance/identifier-standard.md §2). DECLARED here rather than derived from the repo directory name: a rename would otherwise silently orphan every id already issued, and that surfaces much later as unresolvable references with no obvious cause. Reserved spine prefixes (usr/org/prt/app, billing, messaging) belong to FuzeFront; this product's own types namespace as keys_<type>. Enforced by `gate_identifier.py --namespace`.

a2a._note: Secret-broker serving role. FLIPPED enabled:false->true 2026-08-26 on owner instruction. The repo-local card-projection inputs the old note gated on are now COMPLETE: agent-templates/roles/keys-broker/role.json carries a valid `description` (reshaped to the role contract 2026-08-21 — the 'no description' blocker in docs/a2a-tenant-registration.md is stale and is corrected in the same change), providesTo is populated (18 entries; an empty list DENIES every caller per authz.md), and the keys-broker serving role plus the deterministic broker core (backend/app/broker) both exist. WHAT enabled:true DOES: a2a-maintain.yml's preflight now RESOLVES a credential instead of skipping (a declared surface must have a usable LLM credential — proven present, since mcp.enabled:true's fail-closed preflight passed on the same runner in #40), and the a2a-maintainer agent runs on every PR to validate card projection against the frozen contracts/a2a/v1 (in FuzeAgent) and reconcile drift. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not by itself route traffic. The image is ONE shared runtime, `ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuze-a2a` (the `fuzeagent-a2a` name that used to appear here was a stale pre-rename spelling; both currently resolve on GHCR but the contract's authoritative name is `fuze-a2a` — FuzeSDLC governance/a2a-runtime-standard.md). SERVING TOPOLOGY CORRECTED (2026-09-02): this repo now ships its OWN single-tenant A2A pod at deploy/helm/fuzekeys/templates/a2a.yaml, config-only against the shared image — NOT a cross-repo tenant entry in FuzeAgent's a2a-shared server as the prior note here and docs/a2a-tenant-registration.md previously said. That prior plan assumed `agent-templates/a2a/card_generator.py`'s callable endpoint was a hardcoded constant with no per-product override; FuzeAgent#148 (contract v1.2.0) made it read `a2a.inClusterUrl` from the values document instead, so a per-product pod is reachable once deployed. The chart's `a2a.enabled` stays false pending two operator preconditions, neither of which is a code change: the `a2a-provider-anthropic` SealedSecret has not yet been sealed into this repo's own `fuzekeys` namespace, and the fleet Anthropic workspace is separately reporting a low credit balance. SECURITY UNCHANGED: this is a credential vault; the broker never returns raw secret material (only a short-lived derived credential or a decision), high-sensitivity releases are human-gated, and authz is always on the authenticated transport identity.

mcp.note: GATEWAY DIALECT, corrected 2026-08-23 to match what this repo actually deploys. deploy/helm/fuzekeys/templates/mcp-gateway.yaml renders the SHARED OpenAPI->MCP gateway image (ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuze-mcp-gateway) as the `fuzekeys-mcp` pod, mounting copies of contracts/openapi.yaml and mcp/tools.overrides.yaml from deploy/helm/fuzekeys/files/ (kept in step by scripts/sync-mcp-spec.sh --check). deploy/helm/fuzekeys/values-contabo.yaml — the ONLY valueFile the Argo Application (deploy/argocd/applications/fuzekeys-platform.yaml) lists — sets mcp.enabled:true, and has since #65 on 2026-08-10. PRODUCTION STATE, reported honestly: the pod is DEPLOYED AND BROKEN — observed in CreateContainerConfigError on 2026-08-21 (FuzeInfra cluster-query run 32475207623). Deployed-and-broken is still deployed; it is the opposite of the absent surface this block used to claim. WHAT WAS WRONG: this block declared enabled:false with a stdio server at `mcp/server.py`. That file has never existed — the only thing under mcp/ is tools.overrides.yaml, the GATEWAY's override input. THE SECURITY CONSTRAINT FROM THE OLD NOTE STANDS AND IS NOT SOFTENED BY THIS CHANGE: this repo is a credential vault, and a tool that returns a decrypted secret is NOT a read — it must be classified mutates:true (or excluded outright) in mcp/tools.overrides.yaml so it can never be reached as a side effect of a query. That classification is mcp-maintainer's to verify against the live tool list; enabling this flag records where the surface IS, it does not certify that the classification is correct. WHAT THIS ACTUALLY CHANGES DOWNSTREAM — stated from the workflow as it exists today, and NOT from the assumption that flipping this flag turns a check red. IT DOES NOT. .github/workflows/mcp-maintain.yml runs on EVERY pull_request and is gated only on secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; with no key it emits a ::notice:: and the job SUCCEEDS. Nothing in this repo's CI reads mcp.enabled at all — that was checked, not assumed. What the flag really steers is the mcp-maintainer AGENT the workflow runs: its prompt tells it to assess the .fuze/manifest.json mcp block and the servers named in servers[], and to 'never flip enabled:true for a server with no working tool'. With enabled:false pointing at a server file that does not exist, the correct agent behaviour was to read this as a dead scaffold and no-op — so the manifest was steering the maintainer away from a surface that is live in the cluster. THE VACUOUS GATE HERE IS THIS FILE, NOT THE WORKFLOW. Nothing in CI cross-checks the manifest against the chart's effective prod values, which is exactly why the contradiction survived; the gate that would have caught it does not exist yet. `toolCount` and `irreversibleTools` are deliberately NOT declared: nothing in this change booted the gateway against contracts/openapi.yaml, and the schema defines toolCount as a value verified by doing exactly that. mcp-maintainer fills them in from a real run.
